text.p: Shares in brewer Heineken dropped 13.50 guilders to 324.50, after hitting a low of 317.00 earlier after fellow brewer Grolsch announced flat earnings for 1996 and said 1997 earnings were expected to be worse.
Heineken will announce its 1996 results on Friday and analysts have forecast 2.5 percent lower profits, at some 647 million guilders as a result of a cool summer and increased raw material costs.
The Dutch media has reported a drop in local beer consumption in 1996.
"After Grolsch we remain sceptical on Heineken," said one dealer.

"If Heineken says on Friday it still sees good growth potential and an increase in profit margins, it is time to be optimistic again," the dealer said, adding the market was likely to remain cautious until Friday.
"The trend for beer is down, so Heineken has to attract new consumers, one way or the other," she said.
